messages:
Chen: Canary cluster A (dedicated) showed a sudden P95 jump after the adaptive-prefetch-v2 merge — from ~120ms to ~420ms for text-gen workloads. Observed across 3 nodes.
Sara: ugh. Which metric first alerted?
Chen: p95 token latency in the /generate endpoint, plus KV cache hitratio dropped ~18%. Logs show a lot of KV eviction churn.
Mike: I saw the CI perf job fail on nightly perf-run-3 as well. It flagged total tokens/sec down ~25%. Failing job: `perf/canary/latency` with diff > +200ms p95.
Priya: tagging the profiler output I pulled from the canary node. Key snippet:
```
Flame: cpu hotspots: 45% kernel_select(), 22% kv_cache::evict_path(), 12% nvme_io_wait()
Heap: increased allocations in PrefetchQueue::enqueue() after merge
```
Priya: seems the new prefetcher is over-aggressive — it fills the KV prefetch queue and triggers more IO + evictions.
Chen: bisected to commit `c3f9a1b` (merge adaptive-prefetch-v2). Reverting that commit in a test cluster returns p95 to baseline.
Mike: confirmed locally with the smoke harness. Revert fixes tokens/sec and hitratio.
Nina: deploy-bot shows the canary rollout completed at 2026-03-09T09:12Z (deploy-bot: `deploy canary adaptive-prefetch-v2`).
deploy-bot: deploy canary adaptive-prefetch-v2 @ 2026-03-09T09:12Z :white_check_mark:
Sara: is this impacting Dedicated customers right now or only canary?
Chen: only canary observed so far but Dedicated capacity is on the same image tag and would be affected if rollout continues. Risk: SLA p95 target 200ms could be breached.
Priya: quick mitigation options: 1) revert merge on main to stop further rollouts, 2) push hotfix to throttle prefetcher adaptive heuristics (fast to test), 3) config toggle to disable prefetcher per-deployment.
Nina: ops: we should hold the Dedicated rollout and flip the canary back to previous image. Who can cut the revert PR now?
Mike: I'll open the revert PR and request an urgent canary rollback.
Priya: I'll instrument a lightweight prefetch throttle flag and run a micro-canary once revert is in flight. If revert is slow, toggle could be a stopgap.
Chen: adding profiling traces to the canary dashboard: `/dashboards/perf/canary/186345` so we can watch memory + KV eviction rates in real time.
Sara: assign owners: Mike = revert PR + rollback, Priya = throttle branch + micro-canary, Chen = monitoring + postmortem draft. Nina = coordinate customer comms if we need to escalate.
Mike: PR opened: `revert c3f9a1b adaptive-prefetch-v2` -> https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4021
Priya: micro-canary job queued: `ci/micro-canary-prefetch-throttle`
Chen: preliminary root cause hypothesis: adaptive prefetcher changed prefetch window formula and no longer considered live KV occupancy; leads to prefetch storms that evict hot entries and cause NVMe wait amplification.
Nina: holding main rollout until revert lands and canary verifies. Notifying support to pause Dedicated upgrades. @support-team please stand by. :warning:
Sara: good. Keep thread updates short. Once revert lands we run a focused perf-run and decide next steps (fix+re-enable or rewrite heuristics).
Mike: rolling back canary now. will post result shortly. :thumbsup:
(15m later) Mike: canary rollback complete, p95 back to ~130ms, KV hit ratio restored.
Chen: leaving an action item: full bisect log + profiler snapshots into the perf blamestore and a short runbook for future prefetcher flips.
Priya: will prototype a conservative prefetch policy that respects KV occupancy and backpressure; ETA EOD tomorrow for a PR.
Nina: thanks team — holding rollout and informing customers if anything changes.
Sara: filing a short postmortem once we have the revert timeline and perf artifacts.
